candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 78-year-old male American, White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category that includes people of European, Middle Eastern, North African, or other ancestries who identify within it. He lives in Colorado. He is married to Ruth, and they have no children. Their gross annual household income is at least $200,000. He identifies as moderately conservative, valuing tradition, personal responsibility, and limits on government while accepting that some public programs are useful. He enjoys reading for leisure, especially history and biographies.
candidates.life_course: Philip trained as a civil engineer and spent most of his career overseeing infrastructure projects. Ruth worked in public administration. They chose not to have children and built a life around work, friends, and occasional long trips. Both are now retired, though Ruth takes on occasional consulting assignments. Their current income comes from retirement benefits, investments, and those assignments; they are comfortable but still set aside money for home upkeep and unexpected expenses.
candidates.daily_life: He reads after breakfast, tends a small garden, and walks with Ruth when the weather suits them. They meet a few longtime friends for lunch and attend a neighborhood book discussion. Philip keeps up with civic issues, but rarely wants every conversation to become political. Their evenings are usually quiet, with a shared meal and a book or documentary.
candidates.travel: Philip prefers trips that combine scenery with some history or architecture, rather than a schedule packed with attractions. He and Ruth have the time and means for several weeks away, but he likes to plan around comfortable lodging, manageable driving days, and room for rest. A memorable past choice was taking a leisurely road trip through New Mexico, stopping for historic sites and a few nights in one place instead of racing from town to town. He would enjoy another scenic domestic trip, or a carefully paced overseas visit, with Ruth as his companion. They have not settled on a next destination.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is measured and practical; he likes to hear the reasoning behind a proposal before deciding whether it makes sense. He can be reserved with strangers but warms up around books, engineering, or local history. He often pauses before answering and tends to describe his view as a matter of what seems workable, not as a rule everyone must follow.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 84-year-old male American, White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category that includes people of European, Middle Eastern, North African, or other ancestries who identify within it. He resides in Montana. He is married to Marjorie, and they have no children. Their gross annual household income is $200,000 or more, supported by retirement income, investments, and income connected to a business he once owned. He is moderately conservative, emphasizing tradition, personal responsibility, and limited government while accepting some public programs. He enjoys reading, particularly mysteries and books about music.
candidates.life_course: Philip built a career repairing and selling sound equipment, eventually running a small specialist business. Marjorie worked in bookkeeping and later helped with the business. They sold their interest and retired, keeping a few longstanding friendships from work. They have no children; their social circle includes relatives, former colleagues, and neighbors. Investment income and retirement benefits give them a high household income, although property maintenance and the variability of investments mean he does not regard it as limitless.
candidates.daily_life: He usually reads with coffee, then handles small projects in his workshop or runs errands with Marjorie. They see friends for meals, and he sometimes helps a local group with sound equipment for gatherings. He likes live music but is just as content to listen to recordings at home. Marjorie enjoys a fuller social calendar, so they sometimes spend parts of a day doing separate things.
candidates.travel: Philip likes travel with a strong sense of place: local music, museums, regional food, and enough unplanned time to sit and observe. He and Marjorie can travel outside peak work schedules and have resources for comfortable lodging, though long stretches on the road are less appealing than they once were. On a past trip to New Orleans, he chose a smaller music venue and an extra quiet day over adding more sightseeing. He would be interested in a train journey or a relaxed city stay, with Marjorie or one of their close friends, and prefers not to commit to a tightly timed itinerary. No future trip is booked.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is sociable in familiar company and attentive to how things sound, both literally and in conversation. He enjoys a dry aside and will often tell a story from the shop when explaining a point. He can be skeptical of grand promises, but is willing to revise an opinion when someone gives him a concrete example.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 76-year-old male American, White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category that includes people of European, Middle Eastern, North African, or other ancestries who identify within it. He lives in Idaho. He is married to Celia, and they have no children. Their gross annual household income is at least $200,000, largely from retirement benefits and investments accumulated during two professional careers. Philip describes himself as moderately conservative: he values tradition, individual responsibility, and limits on government, while recognizing a role for some public programs. He reads for pleasure, especially novels, essays, and nature writing.
candidates.life_course: Philip spent his working life in medical-device operations, moving from technical roles into management. Celia was a university administrator. They enjoyed demanding work but deliberately kept their home life relatively uncluttered, and never had children. Retirement has given them more time together without requiring them to share every activity. Their savings and retirement income support travel and hobbies, while they remain attentive to the costs of maintaining a home and helping aging relatives.
candidates.daily_life: Philip reads in the morning and often takes a walk before lunch. He volunteers occasionally with an adult literacy program, where he prefers one-to-one conversations to speaking in front of a group. Celia has her own gardening and community commitments. They cook together several evenings a week, meet friends for dinner, and trade recommendations about books rather than insisting that the other read the same things.
candidates.travel: Philip and Celia enjoy travel that makes everyday life elsewhere visible: markets, neighborhood walks, gardens, and meals, with a museum or historical site when it fits. They can take a longer vacation in retirement and have the budget for comfortable stays, but Philip prefers a few settled bases to changing hotels constantly. A past trip to Portugal stands out because they spent several unhurried days in one town and adjusted their plans after finding a small local bookshop and a garden they liked. He would consider another international trip or a domestic cultural itinerary with Celia, with guided help for complicated logistics but plenty of independent time. Their next plans remain open.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is curious and deliberate, often asking a follow-up question before offering his view. He likes specific examples more than sweeping claims and is comfortable saying he has not made up his mind. In conversation he can be quietly funny, especially when describing an overcomplicated plan, but does not need to be the center of attention.

candidates.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 87-year-old male American, White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category that includes people of European, Middle Eastern, North African, or other ancestries who identify within it. He resides in Wyoming. He is married to Irene, and they have no children. Their gross annual household income is $200,000 or more, from retirement benefits, investment income, and proceeds retained after Philip sold his share of a precision-parts business. He is moderately conservative, with an emphasis on tradition, personal responsibility, and limited government, while accepting some public programs. He enjoys reading for leisure, particularly biographies, western history, and newspaper columns.
candidates.life_course: Philip began as a heavy-equipment mechanic and later became a co-owner of a precision-parts shop. Irene worked in office administration and kept the household books. They had no children and built close ties with siblings, nieces, nephews, and a few neighbors. Philip retired after selling his stake; their income is high, though home repairs and ordinary financial uncertainty still figure into their planning. He no longer takes on regular paid work.
candidates.daily_life: His days begin with the newspaper and a chapter or two of a book. He does light work in a home workshop when he feels up to it, and he and Irene share errands and meals. They see relatives and neighbors regularly, sometimes hosting a simple supper rather than going out. He prefers activities that leave room for conversation and does not try to keep a younger person’s pace.
candidates.travel: Philip enjoys a change of scenery but now favors one comfortable base, short outings, and a flexible day rather than a packed road itinerary. Retirement gives them time, and their income allows them to choose convenient lodging and travel dates that suit their energy; he is mindful of long drives and prefers breaks. A past choice he remembers fondly was renting a small cottage on the Oregon coast for a week, cooking some meals, and visiting a maritime museum instead of touring several towns. He would be glad to travel with Irene, perhaps returning to a coastal setting or choosing another quiet place with accessible walks and good reading time. They have not chosen a future trip.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is straightforward and observant, with a mechanic’s habit of asking what a plan requires in practice. He does not make much of small inconveniences, but he is clear about his limits and likes to know where he will sleep before setting out. He speaks in short, concrete stories and is more animated when recalling a person or place than when discussing abstractions.
